scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% versus a 95% target, for 9200 accounts, over period 2026-08..09.

F-02.statement: No tariff changes were recorded in the billing system's tariff change log for the reviewed period.

F-03.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED and 1785 ACTUAL (3025 total).

F-04.statement: Dispute ticket response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2: the utility may request route priority changes, executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log.lagging_routes returned 14 routes below target completion; sample record: route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: Of 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills, 1184 had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected on import for high consumption; 56 had no AMI read received at all and were not exported.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP.statement: Dispute volume doubled because ticket response/handling capacity did not scale, so an AI auto-answer agent would resolve the surge; underlying bill accuracy is not the main issue.

H-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill errors (e.g. wrongly accepting/rejecting reads), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery (H-MDMS-BILL, vendor ORG-AMI) degraded since August, causing more estimate substitutions and incorrect bills that generated disputes.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter reading quality or completeness dropped since August (contracted ORG-FIELD), producing incorrect reads/bills and disputes.

H-EXTERNAL-NON-ERROR-SURGE.statement: Bills issued since August are largely correct, but disputes rose due to a non-error factor (e.g. a legitimate consumption/tariff change customers find surprising), not a billing-pipeline defect.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 accounts — a measurable shortfall in completed manual reads during the dispute-surge period.

re-read under E-11 (accepted premise check) — PR-ROOT: E-11 shows the 'confirmed mechanism' (route completion -> estimate substitution) is wrong for 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-channel disputes, which are AMI-metered accounts whose received reads were rejected by billing import, not accounts lacking a manual read. The doubling, tariff-ruled-out, and 59%-unconfirmed parts of the root statement still stand, but the one 'confirmed' causal claim does not.; PR-CHAIN-2: E-11 shows 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported, then REJECTED by billing import for high consumption - i.e. estimate substitution occurred despite an accepted read, not because route completion left 'no accepted read' as this premise requires.
The billing system's tariff change log shows zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes occurred in the reviewed period that could explain higher bill amounts driving the dispute surge.

Among disputed bills, 1785 (59%) used ACTUAL meter reads and 1240 (41%) used ESTIMATED reads (total 3025), so the majority of disputes attach to bills that were NOT estimate-substituted. This means read-estimate failures (AMI delivery or field-read gaps) explain at most a minority of disputed bills; something else is driving disputes on bills with ACTUAL reads too.

re-read under E-11 (accepted premise check) — PR-ROOT: E-11 shows the 'confirmed mechanism' (route completion -> estimate substitution) is wrong for 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-channel disputes, which are AMI-metered accounts whose received reads were rejected by billing import, not accounts lacking a manual read. The doubling, tariff-ruled-out, and 59%-unconfirmed parts of the root statement still stand, but the one 'confirmed' causal claim does not.; PR-CHAIN-2: E-11 shows 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported, then REJECTED by billing import for high consumption - i.e. estimate substitution occurred despite an accepted read, not because route completion left 'no accepted read' as this premise requires.

CRM dispute response-time data (2440 tickets, median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days) shows tickets are currently being resolved within SLA despite the volume surge, so ticket-handling capacity/speed is not currently failing. This weighs against the surge being explained by handling capacity not scaling, pointing instead toward volume/cause-of-disputes as the driver.

CRM data shows monthly dispute counts of 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug), 1260 (Sep) — confirming that ticket volume roughly doubled abruptly between July and August, matching the stakeholder's claimed timing but adding no information about cause.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year, which agrees with authoritative tool evidence E-02 (empty tariff change log). As a stakeholder statement it is a non-authoritative claim, not new proof, but it corroborates the existing finding that tariff change is not the dispute driver.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager, who has an incentive for a contract headcount increase) claims a shortfall of three meter readers since July causes routes to run late, with affected customers receiving estimated bills. This is an unverified, non-authoritative explanation offered for the route-completion shortfall already measured in F-01/E-01, but it only speaks to the estimate-substitution channel and says nothing about disputes on bills with ACTUAL reads (E-03), which form the majority of disputes.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is an authoritative contract clause establishing that route priority change requests from the utility are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager; it confirms the already-encoded K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint and names SH-FIELD as the confirming authority, but says nothing about the cause of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) identifies 14 individual manual-read routes with below-target completion, sample route R-00 at 0.70 — well below both the 95% target and the 88% aggregate already measured in E-01. This adds route-level granularity showing the completion shortfall is unevenly distributed across routes rather than uniform, but does not by itself establish whether staffing shortage or routing/scheduling inefficiency is the cause.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor engineer) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned as of today per vendor ticket TX-4471, but this is an unverified, non-authoritative stakeholder statement and tool_health still records mdms-export as DEGRADED. If accurate, it would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING query needed to resolve U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL and the DA-MDMS-dependent solution remedy, but it says nothing yet about the actual content of AMI read events or the dispute-surge cause.

AMI read events behind the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (matching E-03's total) show 1184 cases where an AMI read arrived before cutoff and was exported but rejected by billing import for "high consumption," and only 56 cases of no AMI read at all. This points to a billing-import validation-rule rejection as the dominant driver of ESTIMATED-channel disputes, not AMI delivery failure and not (on these AMI-metered accounts) manual-read staffing shortfalls.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-DRIVER.question: What billing-pipeline mechanism explains the 59% of disputed bills that used ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimates?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-DRIVER.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation must target billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) or AMI read accuracy (DA-MDMS); the current root_problem's estimate-substitution mechanism does not cover this majority of disputes.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-DRIVER.resolution_path: Query billing-config validation rule change log (DA-RULES) and cross-reference against disputed ACTUAL-read bills (DA-TICKET) for correlated rule-change dates.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-DRIVER.safe_placeholder: Proceed with diagnostic queries only; defer any bill correction action until the driver is confirmed with evidence.

U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL.question: Do AMI read events (DA-MDMS) show reading errors or inconsistencies for the ACTUAL-read accounts whose bills are disputed?
U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL.decision_impact: Determines whether AMI/MDMS read quality (vendor ORG-AMI) contributes to ACTUAL-read disputes; mdms-export is currently DEGRADED (ACCESS_PENDING) with no fallback, blocking direct verification.
U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL.resolution_path: Await vendor-provisioned mdms-export access (ORG-AMI) to query AMI read events for disputed ACTUAL-read accounts; escalate the ACCESS_PENDING hold if unresolved within the remaining budget.
U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI-read-accuracy diagnosis as unavailable/best-effort until mdms-export access is restored; do not assume AMI error as a confirmed cause.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Is the claimed field reader staffing shortfall actually the cause of the route-completion shortfall, or is routing/scheduling inefficiency responsible?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether route-completion remediation should target staffing or scheduling efficiency, and whether push_route_update is the right lever.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Analyze route-log scheduling patterns independent of the headcount claim (E-07 is testimony from a party with a headcount incentive) before any dispatch change is proposed.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Do not push route updates based on the staffing-shortage claim alone; require independent route-log analysis first.

U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.question: Does raw dispute ticket volume (G-1) adequately capture success, or could it be reduced by faster/auto ticket closure without fixing bill accuracy?
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If ticket volume alone can fall without fixing bill accuracy, M-DISPUTE-VOLUME is an invalid standalone success proxy and must be paired with a bill-accuracy metric.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Pair dispute-volume tracking with root-cause and estimate-share evidence so volume reduction is validated against bill-accuracy findings, not ticket-closure speed alone.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Report dispute-volume trend alongside root-cause evidence; do not treat volume reduction alone as success.

structural_remedies.description: Run the deterministic read-only query_billing_validation_rule_log against DA-RULES to check whether an import validation rule change coincides with August and explains disputes on ACTUAL-read bills.
structural_remedies.rationale: Already in PD-1 intended_scope, read-only, billing-config tool health is UNKNOWN but not reported DOWN, no approval constraint applies (not a protected action).; residual gap: Diagnostic only; even if a rule change is found, the actual config fix/root-cause confirmation for U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-DRIVER still needs to be designed and the VOB closed before release.

structural_remedies.description: Obtain vendor-provisioned export access to DA-MDMS and run query_ami_read_events to check for AMI read errors on disputed ACTUAL-read accounts (U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL).
structural_remedies.rationale: mdms-export tool health is DEGRADED and acquisition explicitly requires vendor provisioning (DA-MDMS), an external dependency that may not resolve within the 225-minute remaining budget even though read-only access is otherwise unrestricted.; residual gap: If vendor access cannot be provisioned in time, VOB-U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL stays OPEN and the majority-mechanism root cause remains unconfirmed before release.

structural_remedies.description: Have SH-FIELD adjust manual-read route scheduling/dispatch and push_route_update (with required runtime confirmation) to restore the 95% completion target and cut estimate substitutions.
structural_remedies.rationale: push_route_update is already an authorized domain action (DA-PUSH-ROUTE-UPDATE) subject to K-DISPATCH runtime confirmation by SH-FIELD, which is a procedural step, not a blocker.; residual gap: Only addresses the confirmed 41% estimate-substitution channel (E-03); the underlying cause of the shortfall itself (staffing vs. scheduling, U-FIELD-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE) is unverified and rests on a biased stakeholder claim (E-07), so the fix may not hold, and it leaves the 59% ACTUAL-read mechanism untouched.

structural_remedies.description: Introduce a change-management process (sign-off + audit log review) for future DA-RULES billing-import validation rule changes to prevent silent, unexplained rule changes from driving bill errors.
structural_remedies.rationale: Pure process/governance change within ORG-UTIL's own authority (billing-config is ORG-UTIL-owned), requires no protected-action approval and no new tooling.; residual gap: Preventive only; H-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE is still CANDIDATE, not confirmed as the actual mechanism, so this does not by itself fix any already-issued incorrect bills or resolve the current 59% unexplained disputes.

structural_remedies.description: Instrument/validate the H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL handoffs (delivery_status, semantic_validity) so data-pipeline integrity between field reads/AMI reads and billing import can be confirmed or ruled out as a contributor.
